items.q: What goes wrong when an agent searches a big corpus with grep?
items.a: Lexical hits have **no relevance**, so the model **reads every document** and token costs climb.

items.q: What is the Frankenstein RAG stack?
items.a: OCR, chunking, one embedding, a vector DB and a reranker, each a vendor and **each step lossy**.

items.q: Why does classic RAG degrade in production?
items.a: One vector per chunk makes **look-alike documents** collapse together, so accuracy **drops as the corpus grows**.

items.q: What does a late-interaction model do differently?
items.a: It keeps **many contextual embeddings** per page and per query instead of **a single vector**.
Charts, tables and layout survive; **OCR loses them**, though it's still kept for **citations**.

items.q: Which search tools should an agent choose between?
items.a: **Grep, normal search, or agentic multi-hop search**, picked by query complexity.

items.q: What happened at the hedge fund with 1B+ documents?
Why did LLM spend fall about 3x?
items.a: Most tokens go to **finding and reading**; better retrieval means **less context**.

items.q: What's the real bottleneck for agents, per Shakir?
items.a: **Access to the right data**, not intelligence.
